subject: Post-demo: data retention exception for PII/transcript logs
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: data retention exception for PII/transcript logs

Hi Aisha — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- What we heard: FinServe needs a way to ensure customer PII tokens and verbatim user inputs are not retained in logs for production traffic (ideally 0-retention for PII / transcripts).
- Redwood options: hosted API default retains limited request/response logs for 90 days for debugging and quality; Dedicated/Private customers can opt for custom retention and internal masking, but we can propose a retention-exception for hosted if acceptable controls are in place.

Ask: can you confirm the exact scope you want 0-retention for (full transcripts, only tokens flagged as PII, all request metadata)? I took the liberty of attaching the meeting notes and your compliance questionnaire you mentioned.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm scope (full transcript vs PII-only) and whether you need legal wording for contract/SAAS terms.
2) We'll draft a retention-exception term and run it with Legal/Privacy (looping in Marissa).
3) If you want, we can provisionally show an implementation approach and timeline (masking + shortened logs) and include it in the SOW.

Attachments: meeting_notes_20270420.pdf

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finserve.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data retention exception for PII/transcript logs

Thanks Camila — great demo. To clarify: FinServe requires that any user-provided PII (names, SSNs, account numbers) be removable immediately after processing. Our goals:

- 0-retention for raw transcripts that contain PII (we can accept aggregated usage metrics but not raw request/response data).
- Audit logs that show success/failure and high-level metrics are OK, but they must not include PII or full user inputs.
- We need an explicit contract clause and an operational description of how Redwood will enforce this (masking, tokenization, or not logging).

I've attached our compliance questionnaire — sections 4 and 7 are most relevant. Can you and your legal team provide a proposed exception or wording? Also: what is the best path for FinServe — do we need Dedicated or can Hosted be patched to meet this?

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Senior Product Security Manager, FinServe Corp
aisha.patel@finserve.com
(212) 555-0789

Attachments: FinServe_compliance_questions.xlsx
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: FinServe compliance Qs — retention exception request (need legal/privacy review)

Marissa — forwarding Aisha's note. Key points: FinServe wants 0-retention for any raw transcripts containing PII; they can accept aggregated metrics. They also want a contractual clause and an operational description (masking/tokenization vs not logging).

Questions for Legal/Privacy:
- Would we be able to offer a hosted retention exception (0-retention for PII) operationally without degrading support/observability?
- Draft wording — short clause the client can sign.
- If hosted is not feasible, confirm that Dedicated/Private is the recommended approach and what the minimum timeline is to onboard.

Suggested starting terms (for discussion):
- Redwood will not persist request/response content identified as PII beyond 0 hours (immediate deletion) for production requests for FinServe bucket(s).
- Redwood will retain non-PII metrics and aggregate usage for up to 90 days for billing and service health.
- Exceptions: debug snapshots only with customer consent & strict access controls; any sampled logs must be redacted.

Can you take point on a short draft? I can share back to Aisha and propose a technical approach (masking + immediate delete).

—
Camila
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinServe compliance Qs — retention exception request (need legal/privacy review)

Camila — thanks for the context. Drafted a short-form retention-exception for hosted customers we can use as a starting point. High level:

- We can agree to a "PII non-persistence" operational control for hosted customers where Redwood identifies and deletes PII-containing content immediately after processing (effective 0-retention), subject to the following constraints:
  * Implementation requires customer to provide clear PII definitions and to mark production traffic as "PII-protected" via a header or separate ingestion path.
  * For troubleshooting, Redwood may create ephemeral debug snapshots that are time-limited (max 7 days) and accessible only to a narrow set of on-call engineers with customer approval.
  * Redwood will continue to store aggregated, non-identifying telemetry for up to 90 days for billing and health monitoring.

I attach a V1 of the draft clause and a short implementation checklist. Operational notes: hosted customers asking for 0-retention add risk to supportability. If FinServe can accept Dedicated (or Private), we can offer stronger guarantees and enclave controls.

Attachments: draft_retention_exception_v1.docx

If this looks good I can turn it into clean contract language and loop Legal proper (we may need a SOW amendment). Would you like me to propose the DocuSign flow?

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data retention exception for PII/transcript logs — proposal

Hi Aisha — looping back with a proposed approach after Legal review. Summary below; full draft attached (see DocuSign link).

Proposal summary:
- Scope: 0-retention for request/response content that contains customer-identified PII when traffic is marked with the header X-FS-PII=true. Non-PII aggregated telemetry retained up to 90 days.
- Operational controls: Redwood will run a PII detection + redact pipeline in-line and delete raw PII content immediately. Debug snapshots permitted only with explicit FinServe approval (max 7 days).
- Implementation: We can deliver hosted retention-exception configuration and test in 2 weeks after sign-off; Dedicated/Private remains the recommended path if FinServe requires stronger isolation and cryptographic controls.
- Contract: short addendum provided — https://www.docusign.com/req/abc123 (draft)

Next steps:
1) Confirm scope (X-FS-PII header approach acceptable?) and whether FinServe will accept ephemeral debug snapshots with approval.
2) If yes, we will send the DocuSign addendum and schedule a technical runbook review (30–45 minutes) to validate the in-line redaction flow.

If you want us to propose alternative wording (e.g., automatic tokenization instead of deletion) we can include that as an engineering option.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
Attachments: draft_retention_exception_v1.docx
